title: Open a digital storefront
summary: Go from an idea to a small, honest online shop for a digital product: validate it, write the page, set up payment and delivery, and write the policies. A learning path, not a promise of sales.
audience: Anyone who wants to sell something digital, such as a guide, a template or a tool.
disclaimer: Education only, not legal, tax or financial advice. Rules about sales tax, refunds and privacy depend on where you and your customers live: check them before you take money.

modules.title: Is there demand?
modules.goal: Know that someone wants it before you build it.

steps.title: Name the problem and the person
steps.why: A product is an answer. Start with a specific person who has a specific problem and is already trying to solve it.
do: Describe the person in three lines: who they are, what they are stuck on, what they have tried.
Write the problem in their words, not yours.

prompts.label: Sharpen the problem
prompts.text: My idea: <idea>. Ask me questions to define the exact person and the exact problem. Then write the problem in one sentence the way that person would say it.

tips: If you cannot find ten people with this problem, narrow or change the idea.
steps.check: You have a person, a problem and the words they use for it.

steps.title: Test demand cheaply
steps.why: Before building, find out if people care enough to act: reply, join a list, or pre-order.
do: Write a one-paragraph description and a simple way to respond.
Show it to at least ten real people in your target group and record what they say.

prompts.label: Honest test message
prompts.text: Write a short, honest message (under 80 words) describing a <product> that helps <person> with <problem>, asking if they would want it and what they would expect to pay. No pressure, no fake urgency.

tips: Interest is not a sale: ask for a small real commitment.
steps.check: You asked ten people and wrote down their answers.

modules.title: Build the shop
modules.goal: A page, a price, a way to pay and a way to deliver.

steps.title: Write the product page
steps.why: The page must answer: what is it, who is it for, what do I get, what does it cost, what if it is not for me.
do: Write the headline, three benefits, what is included, the price and the refund line.
Add real screenshots or samples of exactly what is delivered.

prompts.label: Draft the page
prompts.text: Write a product page for <product> for <person>. Sections: headline, the problem, what you get (a plain list), who it is not for, price, refund policy, three honest FAQs. No hype and no claims of results you cannot prove.

commands.label: Make a product image
commands.text: Make a clean product cover image: title '<name>', subtitle '<one line>', simple shapes, two colours.
commands.where: NEXXUS command bar, in Creation mode

tips: Describe what the buyer gets, not what you hope happens to them.
steps.check: A complete product page draft exists.

steps.title: Choose payment and delivery
steps.why: Use an established payment provider so card details never touch your own system, and deliver the product reliably.
do: Pick a payment provider that supports your country and digital goods.
Decide how the buyer receives the product and how they get help.

prompts.label: Compare options
prompts.text: I want to sell a <product> as a digital download from <country>. List the questions I must answer when choosing a payment provider (fees, taxes handled or not, payouts, refunds, digital goods rules), without recommending one.

tips: Test a purchase end to end before announcing anything.
steps.check: You know how a buyer pays, receives the product and gets help.

steps.title: Write refund, privacy and contact policies
steps.why: Clear policies protect you and build trust. They are also often a legal requirement.
do: Write a plain refund policy, a privacy note saying what you collect and why, and a contact address.
Check the rules for your location before you launch.

prompts.label: Plain-language drafts
prompts.text: Draft a plain-language refund policy and a short privacy note for a small digital-download shop that collects only an email address and payment through a third-party provider. I will have them checked against my local rules.

tips: A policy you cannot honour is worse than none.
This is a draft to check, not legal advice.
